title: Ensemble helper team: config.yaml
description: A helper team: the agents a calling agent can delegate to, and the LLM backends they can run on. Nothing has a default value: every setting is written, except the two that may be left out because leaving them out means 'not used' (an agent's `prompt` and a backend's `api_key_env`).

llm_backends.description: Model endpoints. The key is the backend's name, which an `opencode` agent's model of type `llm_backend` refers to. Ensemble hands the endpoint and key to the agent's CLI for each run, so they are defined only here. `{}` when there are none.

limits.description: Named limits that agents share, such as one model server's concurrency or one subscription's budget. An agent names one with `limit`. `{}` when there are none.

tracker.description: Where the team's tasks come from.

gates.description: Commands a task's work must pass. The key is the gate's name, which a task's `gate` refers to. Defined here so a task names a gate and cannot bring a command of its own. `{}` when there are none.

agents.description: The helper team's agents, one professional each. The key is the agent's name, which the calling agent delegates by. The names are yours.

max_chars.description: Most characters of notes given with one task. Keep it small for a model with a short context.

max_concurrent.description: Most runs at once across every agent that shares this limit.

budget.description: How much all of them together may run in an hour. `type` decides which other settings there are.

type.description: per_hour_tokens: runs may use at most `tokens` tokens in any hour, counted from what each run reports. A run that reports none counts none. Over it, tasks wait and delegations are refused, saying when the next run is allowed.

tokens.description: Tokens, prompt and completion together, in any hour.

type.description: local_markdown: tasks are markdown files in Ensemble's state directory.
per_hour: at most `delegations` runs started in any hour, counted across sessions. Over it, tasks wait and delegations are refused, saying when the next run is allowed.

delegations.description: Runs it may start in any hour.

command.description: A shell command (sh -c) run in the task's working directory after the agent is done. Exit status 0 passes.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the command may run; at the limit it is stopped and the gate fails.

llm_backend.description: How the model is reached. `type` decides which other settings there are.

type.description: anthropic-api: Anthropic's own Messages API. Only a `direct` agent can run on it: OpenCode needs an openai-compatible-api backend, and Claude Code uses your own login.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key, sent as x-api-key. Keys are never written in this file.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.

type.description: openai-compatible-api: any /chat/completions endpoint (llama-server, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, a hosted API).

base_url.description: Where the endpoint is, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key. Keys are never written in this file. Leave it out when the endpoint wants none.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take before the agent's CLI gives up on it.

prompt.description: What this agent is for. Its first line is what the calling agent sees when it lists the team; the whole of it goes into the agent's system prompt: added to Claude Code's own, added to or in place of OpenCode's own (see the adapter's `system_prompt`), and alone for a `direct` agent. Keep it short for small local models. Leave it out and a CLI agent runs on its CLI's own system prompt alone; a `direct` agent then has none.

max_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit for one delegation. At the limit the agent's process is stopped and what it did is returned, marked unfinished.

recall.description: Give the agent, with each task and delegation, the notes the hub's knowledge vault has about it, within the hub's recall limits and `max_chars`. It needs a hub that keeps knowledge (`--hub`). Leave it out and the agent is given no notes; with it, the notes go to whatever model the agent runs on.

limit.description: The name of one of the team's `limits`, in place of `max_concurrent` and `budget`: the slots and the budget are then shared with every agent that names it.

max_concurrent.description: Most delegations to this agent that run at once in a session, background tasks and blocking calls alike; more wait for a free slot. 1 suits a model server that serves one request at a time. Written with `budget`, or not at all when `limit` is.

isolation.description: Where its tasks run. shared: in the project directory. worktree: each task in its own git worktree (.ensemble/worktrees/<id>) on the branch ensemble/<id>, where its work is committed; Ensemble never merges it. Delegations, blocking or in the background, always run in the project.

budget.description: How many runs it may start in an hour: tasks, each gate retry, and delegations, blocking or in the background. `type` decides which other settings there are.

adapter.description: What runs this agent. `type` decides which other settings there are.

type.description: node: an agent a node of a hub server offers. The task and a copy of the files git tracks go to the node; the agent works there in a folder of its own on the node owner's models, and what it changed comes back and is written here, where gates, branches and commits stay. Needs `ensemble login` to the hub, and `compute` for another person's shared node.

hub.description: The hub server, ws:// or wss://.

agent.description: The agent the nodes offer, by its name in their helper team.

nodes.description: The nodes that may run it, as <owner>/<name>, tried in order: the first one connected that offers the agent runs it. `ensemble nodes --hub <url>` lists them.

type.description: codex: the Codex CLI (`codex exec`), run headless in the project on your own login. It brings its own tools and manages its own context; its sandbox is what limits it.

sandbox.description: Codex's own sandbox, passed to --sandbox. read-only: it can only read. workspace-write: it can change files in the project. danger-full-access: nothing limits it.

command.description: The CLI to run: `codex` if it is on PATH, or a path.

type.description: claude-code: the Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`), run headless in the project on your own subscription. It brings its own tools and manages its own context.

model.description: Claude Code's --model: an alias such as sonnet, opus or haiku, or a full model id.

tools.description: Claude Code's own tools this agent may use, passed to --allowedTools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, ..., or a rule such as Bash(git:*). With permission_mode dontAsk anything else is denied. `[Read, Grep, Glob]` is read-only.

permission_mode.description: Claude Code's --permission-mode. dontAsk denies anything not in tools instead of waiting for a person who is not there.

max_turns.description: Most agent turns Claude Code may take for one delegation.

command.description: The claude binary: `claude` if it is on PATH.

type.description: opencode: the OpenCode CLI (`opencode run`), run headless in the project, on one of `llm_backends` or any provider OpenCode is set up for. It brings its own tools and manages its own context.

model.description: Where the model comes from. `type` is `provider` for a model OpenCode is already set up for, or `llm_backend` for one an LLM backend of this config serves.

tools.description: OpenCode permissions this agent is granted: read, glob, grep, list, edit, bash, webfetch, websearch, task, todowrite, ..., or a rule such as bash(git *). Everything else is denied, and OpenCode hides denied tools from the model. `[read, glob, grep, list]` is read-only.

system_prompt.description: What the agent's `prompt` does to OpenCode's own system prompt, the one that teaches the model OpenCode's tools. `append`: the prompt follows it, sent as an instruction file for the run. `replace`: the prompt takes its place, for a small model whose context cannot spare it; it needs a `prompt`. Either way OpenCode adds the environment and the project's AGENTS.md.

max_steps.description: Most agentic steps OpenCode may take for one delegation; at the limit it reports what it did.

command.description: The opencode binary: `opencode` if it is on PATH.

when_none.description: What happens when none of the models in `try` can be used: no backend answers, or none serves its model. fail: the delegation or task fails, saying what each backend answered. wait: a task waits in the queue and is tried again later; a delegation, which someone is waiting for, fails.

model.description: The model id the endpoint serves, as its /models lists it.

context_window.description: Tokens of context the server really runs the model with (Ollama: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH); the loop compacts the conversation before it outgrows them.

type.description: builtin: an agent loop in Ensemble itself, on a model from llm_backends. It reads, edits and runs commands with the tools listed, so no agent CLI needs installing.

try.description: The models it may run on, in order. Each run uses the first whose backend answers and serves it; with one model, it is simply used.

tools.description: What it may do. read, list, grep and glob only look; write and edit change files; shell runs any command in the working directory.

max_steps.description: Most model calls for one delegation; at the limit the loop asks for a final answer.

max_tokens.description: Most tokens of answer per model call.

model.description: The model id the endpoint serves, as its /models lists it.

type.description: direct: a light agent, one chat request straight to an LLM backend with the agent's prompt as the system prompt. No CLI and no tools: it reads and changes nothing, and answers from the task and its context. For cheap work such as summarising, classifying or drafting.

try.description: The models it may run on, in order. Each run uses the first whose backend answers and serves it; with one model, it is simply used.

max_tokens.description: Most tokens of answer; an answer cut off there is marked unfinished.

type.description: provider: a model on a provider OpenCode is already set up for.
llm_backend: models that `llm_backends` serve. Ensemble gives OpenCode the endpoint and key of the one a run uses.

try.description: The models it may run on, in order. Each run uses the first whose backend answers and serves it; with one model, it is simply used.

name.description: The model id the endpoint serves, as its /models lists it.

context_window.description: Tokens of context the server really runs the model with (Ollama: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH), so OpenCode knows when to compact the conversation.
